evaluations.prompt: profile my HIP application with rocprof-compute
expected_behavior: asks for launch command and workload name if missing
runs rocprof-compute profile --name ... -- <app>
validates the workload directory (profiling_config.yaml / pmc_perf.csv)

evaluations.prompt: profile only the gemm kernels in my ROCm app
expected_behavior: uses rocprof-compute profile with -k / --kernel, not --kernel-names

evaluations.prompt: profile my PyTorch application and attribute GPU counters to its operators
expected_behavior: refers to the project Torch tracing documentation
uses --experimental --torch-trace
checks the documented PyTorch installation and version requirements

evaluations.prompt: profile the custom ROCTx ranges in my HIP application with rocprof-compute
expected_behavior: does not claim support for arbitrary user-authored ROCTx range attribution
explains that ROCTx attribution is supported through experimental PyTorch torch tracing
refers to the Torch tracing documentation when the workload is PyTorch

evaluations.prompt: collect rocprofiler-compute counters but skip roofline to save time
expected_behavior: runs rocprof-compute profile with --no-roof

evaluations.prompt: profile my MI300 kernel with stochastic PC sampling using rocprof-compute
expected_behavior: passes --experimental --pc-sampling
sets --pc-sampling-method stochastic

evaluations.prompt: profile with rocprof-compute and keep the raw rocpd database in the workload directory
expected_behavior: uses --retain-rocpd-output and explains profile always uses rocpd

evaluations.prompt: rocprof-compute replay is too expensive; collect a focused set of memory metrics
expected_behavior: uses the named focused metric set fallback
runs --list-sets before selecting --set
states that uncollected analysis panels will be unavailable

evaluations.prompt: profile this destructive one-shot ROCm workload with all counters
expected_behavior: warns that full counter profiling replays the application
does not run until replay safety is resolved
offers a focused metric set when appropriate
